meta.title: How to Find the Next 10x Stock Before Everyone Else
meta.speakers: Eric Jackson (EMJ Capital), interviewed live by Anthony Pompliano
meta.thread_line: 5 threads · Hut 8's Riverbend campus · Opendoor and being early · concentrated book and selling · Bitcoin regime model vs prediction markets · retail leadership and AI research

snapshot: Eric Jackson toured **Hut 8**'s 649-acre Riverbend AI campus in Louisiana and came away calling it *one of the most misunderstood stocks out there*.
His Hut 8 math: ~$10B of borrowing to light the site, roughly $15B of new value created, then recycled into the next campus (Beacon Point, Texas) without equity dilution.
He still backs **Opendoor (OPEN)** after its run from ~70 cents to ~$11 and the pullback since; calls it unfairly punished by the rising 10-year.
Book is ~90% concentrated small-cap growth (Hut 8, Opendoor, Nextdoor, Dave) plus crypto; his biggest mistake is being too early, not being wrong.
His Bitcoin regime model (sold to SRXH, being turned into an ETF) flipped to *stress* at ~$84K a week before the talk and was still there.
New site Event Horizon uses AI to find where Kalshi and Polymarket odds are mispriced: Polymarket gave 3% odds of BTC ending August at $70K; it ended at $79K.
Retail power needs a leader on the soapbox; AI makes research easier but doesn't organise a crowd by itself.

themes.title: Hut 8's Riverbend campus: the coordination game nobody prices
themes.lead: Seeing the site convinced Jackson the AI data-center race is won on coordination and financing, and that Hut 8 is doing both better than most.
bullets: Riverbend: **649 acres**, ~30 minutes north of Baton Rouge, Louisiana; this is only phase one of the first campus, one of ~10 sites Hut plans in Louisiana.
Jacobs is the engineering contractor; a whole section is devoted to Vertiv cooling; Hut has had ~15 people living locally on site since February.
Transformers and substations bigger than he'd ever seen; United Rentals and Caterpillar (CAT) visibly 'making bank', which explains their 5-year stock runs.
Financed with $3.5B of **non-recourse debt** instead of equity, unlike rivals doing $6B dilutive equity offerings.
Total borrowing likely ~$10B; anchor tenant Anthropic via Fluidstack, with Google backstopping financially; his estimate is ~$15B of extra value once the site is lit.
Plan: recycle the $15-20B of created value into the next project, Beacon Point in East Texas, without diluting shareholders.
Local politics was a 'love fest' (Louisiana governor, Don Jr. present), the opposite of the 'everybody hates AI data centers' narrative; CEO Asher Genoot (32) spoke about community, not AI.

themes.title: Opendoor and the SaaS sell-off: when the baby goes out with the bathwater
themes.lead: Jackson's edge is finding stocks the whole market leaned against, then surviving the wait.
bullets: Opendoor ran from ~70 cents (his entry) to almost $11 in a two-month run last year, near the top around September, and has struggled since.
'Nothing's wrong with the stock'; he rates the CEO as hard to beat and blames the ripping 10-year yield for the sell-off.
SaaS was 'supposed to be dead' this year, yet CrowdStrike is up 125% YTD and Twilio up 100%; ZoomInfo is down a lot, so the consensus had 'a kernel of truth'.
Being misunderstood is the shared trait of Carvana and Opendoor before their multi-year runs.
Pompliano's counterpoint: retail investors have been right more than wrong, and Wall Street is now having to follow them.
themes.watch: He publicly campaigned for Opendoor, so his read on it is not neutral; he concedes being 'too early' is his most common error.

themes.title: A concentrated small-cap and crypto book, and the optimist's selling problem
themes.lead: Jackson runs far more concentrated than most would tolerate, and his real filter is timing: is the story about to inflect now?
bullets: Smaller-cap growth names (Hut 8, Opendoor, Nextdoor, Dave) plus crypto make up ~90% of what he plays in.
Dave makes small ~$200 payday-style loans using a Plaid integration.
Biggest mistakes: being right about a story but **two years early**; the test is whether revenue growth is about to jump from 10% to 30%, and why.
Selling starts with knowing yourself: optimists hold too long; he asks whether he misjudged management, was early, or a missed quarter is a blip vs. something ominous.

Daily routine: a morning video first thing (often from 5am), then markets and the 10-year, using AI to trace how rate moves hit Opendoor, Hut and the rest; self-described 'ADHD guy' who hops between problems.

themes.title: A Bitcoin regime model that overrules the bull in him
themes.lead: Jackson's AI model classifies Bitcoin as bull, mixed or stress roughly 30 days ahead, and right now it says stress.
bullets: Models sold to **SRXH** (announced last December, closed in June); this week they announced turning it into an ETF.
May 26: flipped mixed to stress at ~$77K; six weeks later Bitcoin hit ~$58K.
August 14: back to mixed at ~$62K, before a run as high as ~$87K.
A week before the talk, at ~$84K, it flipped to stress again; the human bull in him would have said 'everything's all good'.
During the talk BTC was ~$81.5K; he joked the model might flip back to mixed tomorrow.
Event Horizon, his new site, uses AI models to find where Kalshi and Polymarket are over-bullish or over-bearish: crypto prices, politics, Supreme Court rulings.
Proof point: on August 12 Polymarket gave **3% odds** of Bitcoin ending August at $70K; it ended at $79K.

themes.title: Retail power needs a leader; AI research needs harder questions
themes.lead: AI makes retail research easier than ever, but neither a crowd nor a chatbot does the work without someone stepping up.
bullets: Public-company CEOs now court retail; his basics: be open, authentic, transparent, and hold **video** earnings calls instead of audio-only.
Online shareholder campaigns need leadership like the military or community groups; in his weekly AMAs most people still prefer typing to taking the mic.
Simple prompts ('show me the next Opendoor') waste tokens; better: ask why company A and company B attack the same space differently and who has the edge.
His model ranking: ChatGPT most 'artistic' (tweets, PowerPoints), Claude a solid workhorse without the pizzazz, Kimi best and most thorough for coding and website redesign.

His son Julian (17) pushed the daily videos outside Drake's house for Opendoor to reach people who don't watch CNBC or Bloomberg; it grew into hip-hop business videos (e.g. will Drake re-sign with Universal Music) with a non-investor following now asking about stocks.

takeaways.title: Judge data-center names on financing and execution: non-recourse debt vs. dilutive equity, and how fast a site gets lit.
Before buying a 'right' story, ask whether growth is about to inflect now; being two years early is the costliest error.
When a whole sector gets dumped, sort for the winners instead of exiting the sector.
Write down your selling rules for your temperament; optimists need a mechanical check like a regime model.
Use LLMs for comparative 'why A vs. B' questions, and pick the model per task.
Treat prediction-market odds as a crowd view to test, not a forecast.

glossary.def: A loan secured only by the project's assets, so lenders can't claim the parent company's other assets if it fails.
The main committed customer whose lease makes a data-center campus financeable.
A model that classifies the market state (bull, mixed, stress/bear) rather than predicting a price.
An exchange (Polymarket, Kalshi) where traders buy contracts on outcomes; prices read as crowd-implied odds.
